action: KPMG Canada clients: expect direct contact from KPMG, ask what tax documents were involved, and consider a fraud alert (advice the Credit Counselling Society gave BNN Bloomberg).
date_note: Date KPMG confirmed the incident; the date of the intrusion was not stated.
exec: A major professional-services firm says an outside party reached clients' tax files. Check what you shared with advisers and who holds it.
plain: KPMG Canada says someone outside the firm got into some clients' tax documents. It has not said how many clients or files, or how the intruder got in.

sources.name: The Globe and Mail report via 102.7 WBOW

summary: KPMG Canada confirmed on 18 November that an outside party gained unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents. The Globe and Mail reported it first. KPMG says it has secured its systems and is contacting affected clients, and, in a statement from spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth, that the information is not available online or being misused. It has not said how many clients or files were affected or how the access happened.
title: KPMG Canada confirms unauthorized access to some clients' tax documents

validation.note: Verify desk read BNN Bloomberg (CTV byline) and HRD Canada besides the Reuters copy: both state a third party gained unauthorized access to some clients tax documents and quote KPMG spokesperson Sonja Cloutier-Bosworth; neither gives figures or timing. KPMG own notice and Globe original not read.
